Section 351 generally makes corporate formation nontaxable when requirements are met.
Transferors must control at least 80% of voting stock and 80% of nonvoting stock immediately after the exchange.
Boot can trigger recognized gain.
Liabilities in excess of basis can trigger gain.
Dividends are distributions out of earnings and profits (E&P).

QSBS held more than five years may qualify for gain exclusion.

This module explains when affiliated corporations may file a consolidated return and how consolidated taxable income, compliance, tax years, accounting methods, and liability are handled.

Filing a consolidated return is a privilege for eligible affiliated groups.
The parent must generally own at least 80% of voting power and at least 80% of value.
S corporations, foreign corporations, most REITs, some insurance companies, and most exempt organizations generally cannot join.
Each member is jointly and severally liable for consolidated tax liability, penalties, and interest.

Module Purpose
This module introduces transfer pricing, sourcing rules, foreign tax credit, participation exemption, anti-deferral regimes, GILTI, BEAT, FDII, withholding, residency tests, expatriation, and treaties.
High-Yield Rules

Transfer pricing uses the arm’s-length standard for controlled transactions.
Sourcing rules determine whether income is U.S.-source or foreign-source.
Foreign tax credit is limited to the U.S. tax attributable to foreign-source income.
Participation exemption may allow a 100% DRD for certain foreign-source dividends.
Subpart F and GILTI can cause current U.S. taxation without an actual dividend.
BEAT targets large U.S. corporations with significant deductible payments to related foreign affiliates.
FDII provides a deduction for certain foreign-derived intangible income of U.S. C corporations.

High-Yield Rules

S corporation property contributions generally follow Section 351.
Certain S corporations can still owe corporation-level taxes, including LIFO recapture tax, built-in gains tax, and tax on excess passive investment income.
Shareholder loss deductions are limited by stock basis, debt basis, at-risk rules, and passive activity rules.

Module Purpose
This module covers partnership formation, profits interests, capital interests, partner outside basis, partnership inside basis, debt allocation, built-in gain/loss allocations, loss limitations, tax elections, partner-partnership transactions, guaranteed payments, and nonliquidating distributions.
High-Yield Rules

Contributions of property to a partnership are generally nontaxable.
A profits interest received for services is generally not taxable when received.
A capital interest received for services is generally taxable compensation.
Outside basis tracks the partner’s basis in the partnership interest.
Inside basis tracks the partnership’s basis in its assets.
Recourse and nonrecourse debt allocations can affect outside basis and at-risk amount differently.
Guaranteed payments are deductible by the partnership and taxable to the partner.
Nonliquidating distributions generally reduce outside basis; cash in excess of basis can trigger gain.

Liquidating distributions terminate the partner’s interest.
Basis is generally allocated first to cash, then hot assets, then other property.
Sale of a partnership interest generally creates capital gain or loss, except amounts attributable to hot assets.
Hot assets can convert part of the gain to ordinary income.

Module Purpose
This module covers grantor and non-grantor trusts, simple and complex trusts, trust accounting income, trust taxable income, distributable net income (DNI), beneficiary taxable income, income distribution deduction, and trust taxable income after distributions.
High-Yield Rules

Trust income is taxed either to the trust or beneficiaries depending on trust type, income type, and distributions.
Simple trusts must distribute all income annually, cannot distribute corpus, and cannot make charitable contributions.
Complex trusts are non-grantor trusts that do not meet simple trust requirements.
DNI limits both beneficiary taxable income and the trust income distribution deduction.
Trust taxable income is computed after considering the income distribution deduction.

A Section 501(c)(3) organization must be a corporation, unincorporated association, or trust.
It must have an exempt purpose.

Political campaign activity is prohibited.
Substantial lobbying can jeopardize exempt status.

TCP 4 Module 1 - Nontaxable Dispositions
Module Purpose
This module covers gain/loss calculation, exclusions and deferrals, homeowner’s exclusion, involuntary conversions, divorce property settlements, like-kind exchanges, installment sales, and corporate treasury/capital stock transactions.
High-Yield Rules

Gain or loss equals amount realized minus adjusted basis.
Home sale gain exclusion is up to 250,000 for single/MFS/HOH and 500,000 for MFJ or certain surviving spouses.
The home sale exclusion generally requires ownership and use as a principal residence for at least two years during the five-year period ending on sale.
Like-kind exchange replacement property must be identified within 45 days and received by the earlier of 180 days or the tax return due date with extensions.
Boot received in a like-kind exchange can trigger recognized gain.
Installment sale gain is recognized as cash is received using the gross profit percentage.

High-Yield Rules

Net Section 1231 losses are ordinary losses.
Net Section 1231 gains are generally treated as long-term capital gains, subject to the five-year lookback rule.
Section 1245 recaptures depreciation on business-use personal property as ordinary income to the extent of gain.
Section 1250 applies to business-use real property and generally recaptures excess depreciation over straight-line.
Section 291 can create additional ordinary income recapture for C corporations.

TCP 4 Module 3 - Related Party Transactions
Module Purpose
This module covers related party definitions, constructive ownership, capital gain and loss rules, basis rules, holding period rules, matching of deductions and income, and below-market loans.
High-Yield Rules

Constructive ownership rules can treat stock owned by certain related parties as owned by the taxpayer.

大部分学生都在这两种状态中二选一，很难找到正确的平衡。 配得感低占大多数，表现为：这个岗位太难，我不敢申请；这个公司是大公司，我经验不够；这个笔试我不一定能过，等等等。即使每次我都会苦口婆心的劝说，这些东西往往不是你想的这么难，但是成效并不明显。 眼高手低也占一部分，表现为：即使在还没有找到工作或者哪怕简历市场反应很差的情况，依然不努力的挑三拣四，觉得这个岗位不合适，这个公司不太行。 配得感低的改进方法是请撕掉很多自己无形之中给自己设定的门槛和对职场的滤镜，并且清晰认知到不同岗位到底需要什么技能。禁止自我脑补和想象。 我听过非常多的学生问我 “我这个背景都能申请risk岗位吗？”“难道risk岗位不是需要非常多计算机能力吗？” 她们通常在我反问为什么不行的时候，无法给出任何答案 - 只有一句，“我以为”。这样的“我以为”不基于任何官网信息，也不基于任何从业人员的信息，只是一些随便一听的假设。 只要但凡去官网查一下要求就会知道其实non quant的岗位不需要什么technical，这时，我又会听到：官网写的和实际上要的人可能不是一回事；那么就再进一步去LinkedIn上看看大家进入的背景是怎样的，如果觉得这也可能有包装的成分，那就实际自己多去问几句。多做networking，然后可能就真的了解岗位需求是怎样的。 眼高手低很难劝，因为不自信的人通常能知道自己不自信，但是眼高手低的学生会觉得被pua了。但是眼高手低的学生往往会觉得自己可以如何，但是却不真正付出相应的行动。 “眼高”很好，因为首先要看到要想到才能做到；但是不行动是不行的。我见过很多觉得自己上了某些学校某个专业就已经觉得自己出人头地，公司会抢着要；也见过空口说想要进某某行业，但是从来不付出行动，觉得自己想一想就可以去的。咨询是一个常见的例子，我听过无数学生告诉我想进咨询，如何喜欢，如何合适，但是一旦问起是否有真的做过，或者有真的练习过一两个case，答案基本都是没有的。这样的喜欢未必也太廉价了。没有相对应的行动，就先不要谈结果。 欣赏的状态是：设定一个想要的目标， 然后就开始努力（先不计较得失），边努力边调整预期和方向，确定自己的努力方向正确且坚持。 #北美求职 #offer #2025fall #工作
